- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast peaks >+5% above recent 7-day average, cap at +3% unless sentiment is bullish.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is mixed or neutral.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.50 → -0.33 → +0.50), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% in next 7 days.
